A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AdapTS research work, with 23 complete, readable pages including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original forecasting experiments in Section 5 and Table 1, plus computational comparisons, ablations, and case studies in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains those original forecasting results, computational measurements, ablations, and case studies in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the identical Fourier-domain linear forecaster, Woodbury updates, and fast/slow/merge exponential weighting procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine benchmark datasets and forecasting horizons, and retain the Traffic and cloud time-series case studies in Appendix C.9.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain TTM, TimesFM, VisionTS, Chronos, and Moirai, along with the same continual-finetuning, single-finetuning, and component comparison methods in Appendix C.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices B–C retain identical protocols, including updates every 200 steps, context length 520 with documented model-specific adjustments, horizons 30/96/336, and MASE/RMSSE evaluation.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3–C.7 retain the same update-frequency, frequency-filtering, Woodbury, weighting-component, and forecaster analyses. The distribution-shift illustrations and Appendix C.9 case studies also match.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains identical plus/minus summaries for results averaged across adapted foundation models. Reporting of runs, seeds, uncertainty, and statistical procedures is unchanged throughout both PDFs.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 reports TTM's ETTh1 MASE at H=30 as 0.930, with an AdapTS difference of -0.019, in both versions. Appendix results also remain identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, least-squares and Woodbury derivations, exponential-weighting equations, Theorem 4.1, and Appendix A mathematical reasoning are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about efficient, model-agnostic online forecast adaptation and consistent improvements in the reported experiments.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distribution adaptation, dataset-specific learning, computational tradeoffs, and limitations of infrequent Woodbury updates are unchanged. Appendix C.10 retains the same qualification concerning foundation-model performance ordering.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain identical initialization, normalization, numerical-stability guidance, hyperparameters, warm-up, hardware, and finetuning details. Embedded external-link targets also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and Appendix A.1.2's positioning relative to FITS are identical; no cited works or novelty relationships change.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2502.12920v1 dated 18 Feb 2025 to v2 dated 26 Mar 2025. All paper prose, headings, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All ten figures and seven tables retain identical displays, captions, styling, and placement. Rendered pages match except for the version/date stamp text; layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The full paper and appendices preserve identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, and presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
